perspective:
**Alice Lim’s available information:**

- She knows she is a dental hygienist and knows Austin as an old friend from high school. They have a close friendship and regularly discuss personal and professional lives. She knows her own healthcare experience, friends, and contacts.
- During their coffee conversation, she observed Austin being reserved about work. She invited him to coffee and asked if things were okay at the office. She heard him say it was “nothing really,” just usual ups and downs, then that he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and that it was complicated. She suspected he might be hiding something about his job performance.
- She believed Austin might be considering a career change due to dissatisfaction and felt worried. She asked if he had thought about changing careers and suggested healthcare. She heard him say he had thought about it, didn’t know what other paths to take, asked for her suggestion, and said healthcare sounded interesting and he wanted to learn more about her experiences.
- She sensed Austin was hesitant and afraid of the unknown. She felt frustration and empathy. She told him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. She heard Austin say that was inspiring but he worried about risks and initial struggle. She encouraged him about stepping out of comfort zones and offered support. He thanked her, saying her support and real success stories helped.
- She saw Austin was open to the discussion and felt encouraged and hopeful. She offered to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. He said that would be helpful and appreciated the connections. She said she would set up a meeting next week; he thanked her and said he looked forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, she felt proud, satisfied, and joyful. She believed Austin was ready to take next steps and appreciated her help. She asked how he felt; he said he was excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. She proposed regular check-ins; he agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that her perspective was good.

**Not available to Alice:** the specific details of Austin’s work problems, his actual job performance, his private thoughts or feelings unless he stated them, whether he was truly hiding something, and any hidden or narrator-only facts she did not observe or hear.
